We 'kicked off' with the 100 and this title went to Gerry Leroy, fresh from his annual winter lay-off, who had just a little too much pep for our old friend and former international star Alan Sexton.

…spur Park on June 4th 1949 when the Club did quite well and the result of the Club's coaching methods was clearly seen. Alan Sexton performed a double in winning the 100 and 220 yards and in the latter event he set up a new county record of 22.7 secs.…

Marcus may be interested to know that a Belgravian already has his name on this trophy for Alan Sexton twice won the then 220 yards title in 1948 and 1949, his 22.1 on the latter occasion constituting a AAA Junior record.
The Bels. present were Colin Pearson, Clive Shippen, Alan and Marianne Black, Gordon Biscoe, Pam Davies, Alan Sexton, Ted Pallant, Alan Mead, Jackie Brown and Len and Gill Bishop.

Alan Sexton ran a classic race to win the AAA Junior 220yd title and evergreen Charlie Smart, home on leave from Germany, finished 5th in the AAA 6 mile Championships, only a few yards away from Olympic selection.

We subsequently finished 2nd in the Brockman Trophy with record wins by Bill Lucas in the 3 Miles and Alan Sexton in the 440 yds.
